standard_prerequisites.name: Models of a curve over a discrete valuation ring and smoothness of the special fibre
standard_prerequisites.statement: A model of a smooth projective curve over the fraction field is a flat proper scheme over the discrete valuation ring with that curve as its generic fibre, and it is called minimal when it admits no contraction, equivalently when its numerical type is minimal; the special fibre of a regular model with connected components is connected, and a smooth proper model has smooth connected special fibre. The author's own definitions and the neighbouring lemmas of the same chapter are the allowed inputs.
standard_prerequisites.use: The counted lemma collects the three equivalent formulations of good reduction that the chapter uses when it states its main results on semistable reduction.

core_obligations: First implication: if a smooth proper model exists, then its special fibre is connected and smooth, hence irreducible, which immediately forces the model to be minimal; so the existence of a smooth proper model gives a smooth minimal model (source lines 6427-6430).

Second implication, positive genus case: if the genus of the curve is positive then the minimal model is unique, so the smooth minimal model supplied by the previous step is the only one and every minimal model is smooth (source lines 6431-6434).

Second implication, remaining case: if the minimal model is not unique, then the special fibre of any minimal model is isomorphic to the projective line over the residue field, which makes the model smooth over the discrete valuation ring, and the equivalence follows (source lines 6434-6439).

proof_roadmap.step: From a smooth proper model to a smooth minimal one, using connectedness and smoothness of the special fibre.
Positive genus: uniqueness of the minimal model makes the smooth one the only one.
Non-unique case: the special fibre is a projective line, hence every minimal model is smooth.
